clue.text: Item of furniture not wonky — I had wedge finally stuck in

indicators.note: stuck in says the short pieces are pushed into the middle of the steady word

parts.note: something not wonky is stable
I had contracts to I'd

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word wedge

explanation.surface: Someone props up a wobbly piece of furniture with a wedge until it stops rocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts the two short pieces, I'D and the E ending wedge, into the middle of the word for steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A side table is a small piece of furniture placed beside a sofa or against a wall.

clue.text: He is fantastic with sampan — demonstrating this?

definitions.text: He is fantastic with sampan — demonstrating this?

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters of the words before and after are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boatman handles his small Chinese boat brilliantly, showing off his skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: rearranging HE IS SAMPAN gives the skill a man fantastic with a sampan would display.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling a boat is the craft of a sailor, which someone brilliant with a sampan shows.

clue.text: One cannot see a top marksman

definitions.meaning: a blind eye, one with no sight, is a dead one
a crack shot who rarely misses

explanation.definitionFit: A dead eye is a sightless eye, and the same phrase names an expert shooter with deadly aim.

clue.text: Beginning to tango? Study step

indicators.note: Beginning to asks for the opening letter of the dance named next

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A dance student, starting the tango, studies the steps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'step' towards dancing, but it means a footfall or the flat part of a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstep can be called a tread, as can the flat surface of each stair.

clue.text: Architect beginning to build, say, on green site

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to say is to utter
a field is a grassy site

explanation.surface: An architect starts building on a greenfield site.
explanation.walkthrough: William Butterfield was a Victorian Gothic Revival architect, designer of Keble College, Oxford. 'on' joins the pieces in order down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: William Butterfield was a leading English architect of the Gothic Revival in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: A corny bit from the organ

definitions.meaning: the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant such as maize
the body part used for hearing

explanation.definitionFit: An ear is the grain-bearing spike of corn, and also the hearing organ on the side of the head.

clue.text: Bad fellow from another world who needs to be properly trained?

definitions.text: who needs to be properly trained?

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
ET is the extraterrestrial, a being from another world

explanation.surface: A badly behaved alien visitor needs some proper training.
explanation.definitionFit: A military or police trainee is still learning, so needs proper instruction before service.

clue.text: One of the vegetables to arrive in yard before the end of June

indicators.note: in places the verb for arriving within the word for an enclosed yard

parts.note: a courtyard, or court, is an enclosed yard
to get somewhere is to arrive

indicators.note: the end of asks for the final letter of the month named

explanation.surface: A gardener expects vegetables to turn up in the yard before the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the verb inside the yard, and the final letter of June follows; 'before' only orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette, called a zucchini in America, is a green summer squash eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Like some divers in river — note each going under

indicators.note: going under in a down answer places the following pieces beneath, after the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: Divers in a river note something lurking under each of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. In a down clue, pieces 'going under' another come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers who descend far below the surface of the ocean work in the deep sea.

clue.text: Carry something on pole, not quite getting to the end

indicators.text: not quite getting to the end
indicators.note: not quite getting to the end says the word stops one letter short of its finish

parts.note: a totem is the carved figure on a totem pole

explanation.surface: Someone carries a load on a pole but can't quite make it to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite getting to the end' takes the M off TOTEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is an informal verb for lugging or bearing something around.

clue.text: Saw notice with only half the meeting's items

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice

indicators.note: only half keeps just the front three of the six letters for the list of business

parts.note: an agenda lists the items to be dealt with at a meeting

explanation.surface: An announcement went out covering only half of what the meeting was meant to discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a proverb, not a past tense or a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, a maxim handed down.

clue.text: Old city beast cut short in temporary accommodation, raging

indicators.note: in places the old city and the shortened animal inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: cut short says the animal loses its final letter

parts.note: a bull is a large beast

explanation.surface: An animal from an ancient city is shut in a tent and goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final letter of the animal; 'in' puts the old city and the clipped beast inside the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent seas or crowds are wild and violent, raging in disorder.

clue.text: Cow dung area's been swilled

indicators.note: swilled means sluiced or slopped about, so the letters of the words before are churned up

explanation.surface: A muddy cowshed has been hosed down after the cattle left their mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swilled' rearranges DUNG AREAS BEEN, the possessive's S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of hornless black beef cattle.

clue.text: With this innocence party will lose its core members

definitions.text: With this innocence party will lose its core members

parts.words: With this innocence party will lose its core members
parts.note: read as a word game: the middle of the word party is the letters A, R, T, so being without them strips party to its outer pair; the answer also means naivety

explanation.walkthrough: 'innocence' is the definition; the rest jokes that a party lacking its core members is literally devoid of the letters ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of guile or craft is a state of simple naivety and innocence.

clue.text: Need for tot to be trained as a novice

indicators.note: to be trained means to be shaped and drilled, so the letters are re-formed

explanation.surface: A small child needs to be taught, being a complete beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be trained' rearranges NEED FOR TOT; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is an inexperienced newcomer, originally a greenhorn in the American West.

clue.text: The woman repeated phrase for the officer

parts.note: she refers to a woman
a riff is a short musical phrase played over and over

explanation.surface: A woman keeps repeating a phrase meant for a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riff' is the musical term for a repeated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a law-enforcement official, in America the chief officer of a county.

clue.text: One man's fateful day as leader of army

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name, here with the possessive S
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was murdered

explanation.surface: A general recalls the fateful day he took command of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell, who led the Parliamentarian army in the English Civil War, was nicknamed Old Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell, commander of the New Model Army, earned this nickname for his toughness.

clue.text: Use indicator maybe to measure bird speed

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A naturalist uses a gauge to measure how fast a small bird flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indicator' here is a chemical one, as in litmus, not a crossword signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, one finds a solution's concentration by adding reagent until an indicator changes colour.

clue.text: Put by to rinse having got messy

indicators.note: having got messy means the letters are left in a jumble and must be sorted

explanation.surface: Something set aside to rinse has got dirty in the meantime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having got messy' rearranges TO RINSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve for later is kept stored away, waiting in the wings.

clue.text: Division created by religious group at home, being without love

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: being without means standing outside, so home's word goes round the letter for love

parts.note: in means at home
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A split arises when a religious group, staying at home, finds itself loveless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being without' means standing outside, so the word for home goes round the letter for love. The surface wants 'without' to mean lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is one of the parts something is divided into.

clue.text: Queen receives this person, a lord heartless as stone

indicators.note: receives means the queen's letters take in the speaker's word

parts.note: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
the speaker of the clue is me

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of lord are removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The Queen receives a cold-hearted lord with a face like stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts the speaker inside the royal cipher; 'heartless' leaves only the first and last letters of lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a precious green gemstone.

clue.text: Sue's mad, loony — that can be taken for granted

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the name with its possessive S is used as letters

explanation.surface: Someone declares that Sue is plainly mad, as if that is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' rearranges SUES MAD, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: What is assumed is supposed true without proof, accepted as given.

clue.text: She's scared pin may be wrong — rendering this ineffective?

definitions.text: She's scared pin may be wrong — rendering this ineffective?

indicators.note: may be wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: the pronoun with its contracted verb is used as letters

explanation.surface: A woman at a cash machine fears she has forgotten her PIN.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay: 'may be wrong' rearranges SHES SCARED PIN, and a wrong PIN makes the machine useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine pays out banknotes only when the correct PIN is entered.

clue.text: She's terrified — this chemical has been swallowed

indicators.note: has been swallowed says the answer lies inside the phrase before it, taken in by its letters

explanation.surface: A woman is terrified because she has swallowed a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the words: shE'S TERrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters are organic compounds formed from an acid and an alcohol, often fruity in smell.

clue.text: Half the archbishops may be stiffly correct

indicators.note: Half keeps only the first four of the eight letters of the word for senior bishops

parts.note: the leading archbishops of a country, such as Canterbury, are called primates

explanation.surface: Half the archbishops are rather starchy and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIMATES halved gives the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prim is formal and proper to the point of prudishness.

clue.text: Indra can change ultimately — as a result of this moving?

definitions.text: Indra can change ultimately — as a result of this moving?

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of change

explanation.surface: The Hindu god of rain might change his mind if people perform the right ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: Indra is the Hindu god of rain. 'moving' rearranges INDRA CAN, 'ultimately' adds the last letter of change, and the whole clue describes a ritual meant to sway the god.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed to bring down rainfall might sway a weather god.

clue.text: Make a mistake, getting university type upset

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned over, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A university lecturer blunders and gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DON over; to nod is to slip up, as in 'even Homer nods'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to lapse momentarily through inattention, as in the saying that even Homer nods.

clue.text: Work experienced the wrong way on account of speed

indicators.note: the wrong way says both pieces are read backwards as one run

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
to have met with something is to have experienced it

explanation.surface: Work was done the wrong way because of the haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns both pieces round as a single run; 'on account of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace or rate at which music or activity proceeds.

clue.text: More than one soul gets by without silver

indicators.note: without says the symbol for the metal is taken out

parts.note: someone who manages gets by
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A poor soul scrapes a living without any money.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AG from MANAGES gives the Latin word for spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman religion the deified spirits of dead ancestors were honoured as household ghosts.

clue.text: Record bloody, the thing to bring shame

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
blood-coloured is red
it means the thing

explanation.surface: A gory record is just the sort of thing to cause disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their good name and reputation.
